title: Cross-runner Compatibility Checker and Profile Sanity Validator for Model Onboarding
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Add a deterministic compatibility checker and profile sanity validator to the benchmark harness so that model onboarding and version pinning produce reproducible, trustworthy performance profiles across heterogeneous eval runners and dataset variants.

Background: During model onboarding we've seen noisy profile publishes due to divergent runner implementations (micro-batching differences, tokenization edge-cases, seed variance in sampled prompts) and missing metadata in published profiles. This ticket builds a lightweight cross-runner compatibility layer and a pre-publish sanity validation step that detects common causes of profile drift and rejects or annotates profiles that don't meet reproducibility thresholds.

Goals:
- Surface runner-level incompatibilities early (tokenization mismatch, pre/post-processing differences, unsupported prompt constructs).
- Enforce deterministic seeding and document seed provenance for sampled prompt families.
- Validate key perf metrics (p50, p95 latency, tokens/sec, token-cost) across at least two runner implementations before profile publish.
- Provide automated corrective suggestions (normalization steps or fallback runner mappings) and publish enriched profile metadata for downstream routing and pinning decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A compat-check tool run exists that compares outputs/metrics between two runner implementations for a model and returns a pass/fail + diagnostics JSON.

The harness rejects profile publish if output divergence > threshold (default 2% accuracy delta or configurable) or if latency variance exceeds SLO-defined bounds, unless explicitly overridden with documented rationale.
Seed provenance is recorded in profile metadata (seed, RNG algorithm, sample id mapping) and surfaced in published artifacts.
Dashboard has a new 'Profile Sanity' panel showing last N publishes, pass/fail, and top divergence reasons per model version.
End-to-end tests exercising tokenization mismatch, batch-shape variance, and seeding drift are added and green in CI.
Documentation (confluence + quickstart) updated with how to interpret compat-check diagnostics and how to remediate common failures.
design_notes: Introduce a small compat-check binary in harness/bin that accepts two runner endpoints and a profile candidate; it streams a bounded set of sampled prompts and compares structured outputs + perf metrics.

Compatibility model: compare both semantic outputs (using existing rerank/embedding similarity thresholds) and deterministic fields (structured outputs, function-call args) with two tolerance bands (strict for structured data, soft for free-text).
Use existing seedbank service (seed provenance) to lock sampling; add a compact mapping artifact that maps sample indices to original dataset rows to aid reproducibility.

Publish enriched profile metadata as a separate artifact (profile-meta.json) that includes runner-signature, tokenizer-hash, sample-seed, and compat-check summary to avoid overloading main profile blob.
Design the compat-check as idempotent and cheap: default sample size 128 per profile candidate; configurable per project.
technical_decisions: Use 64-bit deterministic Xorshift+ variant already used in seedbank to guarantee cross-language seeding parity.
Compute semantic similarity using embedding-based cosine with threshold 0.87 for free-text acceptance; structured outputs require exact-match with canonical normalization pipeline.
Runner signature includes (model-variant-id, tokenizer-hash, compile-flags, batch-shape-capabilities). Compat-check fails fast if tokenizer-hash differs unless mapping rules exist.
Integrate compat-check as a pre-publish hook in the harness release pipeline; failure can be overridden by 'force-publish' with documented rationale and email notification to onboarding@redwood.com.

test_plan: Unit tests for tokenizer-hash generation and mapping rules.
Integration test: run compat-check between python-runner and rust-runner using a seeded sample (golden fixture) and assert pass.
Chaos test: introduce intentional tokenization mismatch and assert compat-check returns clear diagnostics and suggested remediations.
Performance smoke: ensure compat-check run for default sample size completes under 30s on CI runner.
rollout_plan: Ship compat-check as opt-in flag in harness (opt-in=default false) for first canary week.
Enable in 'onboarding' CI pipeline for all new model submissions after 1 week of canary if stable.
Add automated email alert to one offcall and owner on first fail; escalate to model-onboarding channel if repeated.
risks: False positives from semantic comparator on short prompts could block valid publishes; mitigation: adjustable thresholds and override policy.
Compatibility mapping for tokenizer differences might become a maintenance burden; mitigation: record mapping rules in repo and limit exceptions.
Extra pre-publish time could slow onboarding; mitigation: small default sample size and optional asynchronous full-coverage checks.
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the tokenization normalization proposal in the proto; rust/python parity tests included in PR.
We intentionally chose embedding threshold conservative to reduce false negatives; product should review tolerances for allowable drift.
Review the force-publish override wording and notification recipients in Launch playbook.
release_notes_blurb: Added a cross-runner compatibility check and profile sanity validator to the benchmark harness. This prevents noisy profile publishes by detecting tokenization, seeding, and runner-signature mismatches before a profile is published and records seed provenance for reproducibility.
